children: Land Securities said it would buy a shopping mall in the U.K. for 516 million pounds, equivalent to $684.4 million, and conducted an equity raise worth around 500 million pounds to fund the purchase.
The real-estate investment trust--which already owns a number of shopping malls, including Bluewater in Kent--said it has agreed to buy Metrocentre in Gateshead, near Newcastle.
Metrocentre is a top-10 shopping mall in the U.K. by sales, with estimated annual retail sales of around 650 million pounds, Land Securities said.
Based on in-place net rental income--a measure of income from existing rental leases--of 41 million pounds, the deal implies an in-place net rental income yield of 7.9%.

Land Securities said the equity issue, which was conducted via an accelerated bookbuild, will partially fund the Metrocentre acquisition, as well as the further consolidation of the company's interests in its existing retail portfolio for around 100 million pounds.

Land Securities placed 81.8 million shares at 600 pence each via the placing, retail offer and subscription. The price is a 3.0% discount to the middle market price of 618.50 pence at the time it was agreed.
Land Securities expects the acquisitions and equity issue to be accretive to earnings per share in the first full year of operation.
The company said it has continued to see strong customer demand over the five months to the end of August, with lettings "comfortably ahead" of estimated rental value.
Land Securities said it is well placed to deliver around 5% compound annual growth in EPS through to fiscal 2030.
